_note: Insurgent presence: armed groups operating or governing rural areas without holding territory outright. Drawn at province or district level, so these are indicative extents, not lines.

presence.name: Southern and central Somalia
presence.note: Holds much of the countryside and taxes trade even in government-held towns; estimates put its control at around 30% of Somalia's land.

sources.title: War on the Rocks: Flailing State, the resurgence of al-Shabaab

presence.name: Kachin State
presence.note: The KIA holds much of rural Kachin State and several towns, and is pressing junta positions around Bhamo; the junta holds Myitkyina.

sources.title: Myanmar Peace Monitor: The junta's campaign to recapture resistance-controlled towns

presence.name: Chin State
presence.note: Chin resistance forces hold most of the state's towns and countryside.

presence.name: Sagaing and Magway
presence.note: People's Defense Forces loyal to the National Unity Government contest much of the dry zone; the junta imposed martial law on dozens of townships here in April 2026.

sources.title: Malay Mail: Myanmar junta imposes military control over 60 townships (April 2026)

presence.name: Karenni (Kayah) State
presence.note: Karenni resistance forces hold much of the state, though the junta has retaken some towns since 2025.

presence.name: Karen (Kayin) State
presence.note: The KNU and allied forces control large rural areas along the Thai border.

presence.name: Central and western Mali
presence.note: JNIM controls much of the countryside, besieges towns, and blockaded fuel supplies to Bamako in late 2025.

presence.name: Northern and eastern Burkina Faso
presence.note: JNIM operates across roughly half of Burkina Faso, blockading many towns that the junta nominally holds.

presence.name: Ménaka, Gao, Tillabéri and Tahoua
presence.note: Islamic State Sahel dominates the Ménaka region and the borderlands of western Niger.

presence.name: Kidal region
presence.note: Tuareg separatists lost Kidal town to the army in 2023 but remain active in the desert, notably around Tinzaouaten.

presence.name: Lake Chad and northern Borno
presence.note: ISWAP holds the Lake Chad islands and much of northern Borno's countryside.

presence.name: Sambisa and the Mandara Mountains
presence.note: Boko Haram's JAS faction operates from the Sambisa forest and the Mandara Mountains.

presence.name: Amhara
presence.note: Fano militias have fought the federal government since 2023 and hold much of rural Amhara.

presence.name: Cabo Delgado
presence.note: Islamic State Mozambique remains active despite Rwandan and Mozambican operations.

presence.name: Northwest and Southwest Cameroon
presence.note: Anglophone separatists have fought for an independent 'Ambazonia' since 2017.

presence.name: Former tribal areas
presence.note: The Pakistani Taliban has resurged in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's former tribal districts since 2021.

presence.name: Balochistan
presence.note: Baloch separatists stage frequent attacks across the province, including the 2025 Jaffar Express hijacking.

presence.name: Catatumbo and Arauca
presence.note: The ELN has dominated these border departments since its 2025 Catatumbo offensive.

presence.name: Cauca and Guaviare
presence.note: FARC dissident factions control rural areas and coca routes.

presence.name: Ouest and Artibonite
presence.note: The Viv Ansanm gang coalition controls most of Port-au-Prince and much of the Artibonite valley.

presence.name: Upper Nile and Jonglei
presence.note: Fighting between the government and opposition forces resumed in 2025 after Riek Machar's arrest.

presence.name: Beni, Lubero and Ituri
presence.note: The Islamic State-affiliated ADF carries out frequent massacres of civilians.
